transcript.text: Good morning, everyone. We've got fourteen 55-gallon drums of spent coolant from the machining area staged in the waste staging area on spill pallets, and the disposal vendor is still waiting on our authorization before they can pick up. I need to run the round-robin review with lab quality, waste logistics, and warehouse supervision before I can approve the disposal route and shipment controls. Can we get representatives from each of those areas together so we can walk through the waste-authorization process and get this moving?
transcript.speaker: A1

transcript.text: I need to flag something important before we proceed. My laboratory analysis on these drums found 2.4% chlorinated solvent in the spent coolant. Per our site's waste matrix, any batch at or above 1.0% chlorinated solvent must go to hazardous-liquid treatment rather than ordinary coolant recycling. I completed this analysis yesterday, but the result hasn't yet been attached to the waste authorization. This will need to be factored into the disposal route decision.
transcript.speaker: A2

transcript.text: I need to share something critical for the shipment planning. I confirmed with our disposal contractor that their tanker permit allows a maximum of 8 of these drums per load, so the 14 drums will need to be split into two shipments: one load of 8 and a second load of 6. I received this permit condition in the contractor's service email, but I haven't entered it into the transport booking system yet. We'll need to account for this in the shipment controls and scheduling.
transcript.speaker: A3

transcript.text: I need to flag an urgent warehouse condition before we finalize anything. During my warehouse inspection, I found active seepage at the base of exactly 4 of the 14 drums. Those 4 drums must each be placed in a UN-rated overpack before any movement, while the other 10 can remain on their existing spill pallets. I recorded this on the shift clipboard, but I have not yet updated the waste file, so this hasn't been reflected in the authorization paperwork.
